title: Coefficient-compatible finite-cover lattice presentation on a normal base
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Suppose that every local ring is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $X$, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] let $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$, with constant sheaves interpreted as sheafifications of constant presheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and put $R_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Let $A_X^{\mathrm{cts}},E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}$ be the continuous-function coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients]. A lisse module means a sheaf module pro-etale locally free of finite rank, including rank zero [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

The underlying space of $X$ is Noetherian and $X$ is quasi-separated. There are canonical ring-sheaf isomorphisms $A_X^{\mathrm{cts}}\cong B_X$ and $E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}\cong B_X[1/\ell]\cong R_X$, respecting the integral inclusions, reductions and localizations.

For every lisse $R_X$-module $L$, regard $L$ as an $E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}$-module through these isomorphisms. For $U\to X$ let $\mathscr L_L(U)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(M,\alpha)$ consisting of a lisse $A_U^{\mathrm{cts}}$-module and an isomorphism $\alpha:E_U^{\mathrm{cts}}\otimes_{A_U^{\mathrm{cts}}}M\cong L|_U$, with classes and restrictions as in [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant]. Tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and restrictions are pro-etale inverse images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then $\mathscr L_L$ is a locally constant, locally nonempty sheaf of sets. On any trivialization $L|_U\cong (E_U^{\mathrm{cts}})^r$ it identifies with the constant sheaf on $\operatorname{GL}_r(E)/\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$, the right cosets of invertible matrices, for every $r\geq0$. There is a finite etale surjection $p:Y\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-surjective-morphism] and an actual representative $(M,\alpha)$ of an element of $\mathscr L_L(Y)$. Equivalently it gives a lisse $B_Y$-module $M$ with $M[1/\varpi]\cong p^{-1}L$ under the same coefficient identifications. No descent datum on $M$ is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; Lemma 7.3.9 and proof of Lemma 7.4.10, pp. 67–71. Intermediate lattice-class construction, with the coefficient and qcqs checks of returned proof steps 1–4.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $X$ is quasi-separated, since it is locally Noetherian. To check the underlying topology, apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] using local Noetherianity and quasi-compactness. Given a descending chain of closed subsets, choose a minimal member of its set of values. Every subsequent member is contained in that member and hence equals it. Thus the chain stabilizes, which is the definition of a Noetherian space.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-completion] on $X$ with the specified finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Its finiteCoefficientRing at index $n$ is the lifted quotient $A/(\varpi^{n+1})$, so its finiteCoefficientLimit is exactly $B_X$, with the positive indices reindexed by $n+1$. Its displayed projection equation says that the image of a continuous integral section at level $n+1$, evaluated at any point, is its residue modulo $\varpi^{n+1}$. Its constant-section equation identifies the constant quotient sheaf with continuous functions to that discrete quotient. Consequently it gives the canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism $i_X:A_X^{\mathrm{cts}}\simeq B_X$, preserving every reduction, including the image of each constant coefficient. This uses the normalized statement, rather than an unnormalized existence of an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58–59: inverse limit of the positive uniformizer-power quotient sheaves

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-localization]: its integralCoefficientLocalization is the sheafification of sectionwise localization at the constant uniformizer, and integralCoefficientLocalizationNormalized says that the map to $E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}$ sends every integral numerator to the same continuous function. Thus it identifies $(A_X^{\mathrm{cts}})[1/\varpi]$ with $E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}$ compatibly with integral inclusion. Localize $i_X$ and its inverse to obtain $E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}\simeq B_X[1/\varpi]=R_X$. For completeness, [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], clause 5, writes $\ell=u\varpi^e$, where $u\in A^\times$ and $e>0$: positivity follows from $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$ and $0<|\varpi|_E<1$. In any $A$-algebra, inverting $\varpi$ therefore inverts $\ell$; conversely $\varpi^{-1}=u\varpi^{e-1}\ell^{-1}$ after inverting $\ell$. These inverse fraction maps identify the two sectionwise localizations and their sheafifications, proving $B_X[1/\ell]\simeq R_X$. The maps fix $B_X$, so they respect its integral map and the already fixed reductions.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(2), p. 59; equality of localization at ell and at a uniformizer follows from the cited DVR factorization

proof.text: Regard $L$ as an $E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}$-module using the inverse coefficient isomorphism just obtained. A local basis $R_U^r\simeq L|_U$ then becomes a basis $(E_U^{\mathrm{cts}})^r\simeq L|_U$ by sending each coefficient through the ring isomorphism. Applying its inverse gives the inverse basis map. Hence $L$ is locally free of finite rank over the continuous rational coefficient sheaf. This argument preserves the original trivializing cover and includes $r=0$.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3 and Lemma 6.8.2: express the same finite local bases through the coefficient isomorphism

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant] to this finite locally free $E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}$-module. Its $A_X(V)=C(|V|,A)$ and $E_X(V)=C(|V|,E)$ are precisely our continuous coefficient sheaves; the isomorphism relation includes the specified rationalization $\alpha$, and its restrictions are exactly the ones in the item. It says that $\mathscr L_L$ is a sheaf and, on every rational trivialization of rank $r\geq0$, identifies it with the sheafification of the discrete right-coset set $\operatorname{GL}_r(E)/\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$. Thus it is locally constant, with exactly the asserted cosets and all ranks allowed.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), proof on p. 60: lattice classes and the constant right-coset sheaf

proof.text: On each member $U$ of the trivializing cover, take the identity coset in $\operatorname{GL}_r(E)/\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$. Under the normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant] it gives the actual pair $((A_U^{\mathrm{cts}})^r,\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ sends the scalar-extended standard basis to the chosen rational basis of $L|_U$. This supplies a section of $\mathscr L_L(U)$ on every member of that cover, proving local nonemptiness. For $r=0$, both matrix groups and their coset set have one element and this pair is $(0,0\simeq0)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), proof: the standard lattice in each rational frame

proof.text: Now apply [lem-a1-normal-locally-constant-finite-section] with $F=\mathscr L_L$. The scheme is nonempty and connected by assumption, locally Noetherian and quasi-compact by the stated meaning of Noetherian, and all its local rings are integrally closed domains by assumption. Steps 5 and 6 give respectively its locally constant sheaf and locally nonempty hypotheses. Obtain a finite etale surjection $p:Y\to X$ and $c\in\mathscr L_L(Y)$. By the definition of the set in [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant], $c$ is an isomorphism class of actual pairs; choose a representative $(M,\alpha)$ in that class. It consists of a lisse $A_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}$-module and an isomorphism $E_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}\otimes_{A_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}}M\simeq p^{-1}L$, exactly as required. Choosing a representative of this quotient class adds no descent datum.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9 and proof of Lemma 7.4.10, pp. 67–71, through the existing finite-section lemma; Proposition 6.8.4(6) for the meaning of the class

proof.text: Apply the same normalized completion and localization statements on $Y$; both are stated for every scheme, so no new finiteness hypothesis on $Y$ is needed. They give $i_Y:A_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}\simeq B_Y$ with its projection and constant-section equations, and identify $A_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}\to E_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}$ with $B_Y\to B_Y[1/\varpi]$. These identifications on $Y$ are the pullbacks of those on $X$, which is what makes $p^{-1}L$ the same module for both coefficient structures. Since $p$ is etale, [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients] makes the comparisons $p^{-1}A_X^{\mathrm{cts}}\to A_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}$ and $p^{-1}E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}\to E_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}$ the identity on continuous functions, and [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], applied to the system $Q_n=A/\varpi^n$, gives $c_p:p^{-1}B_X\simeq B_Y$ with $\pi_{Y,n}\circ c_p=c_{p,n}\circ p^{-1}\pi_{X,n}$, where $c_{p,n}$ sends each constant section to the same constant. The two maps $p^{-1}A_X^{\mathrm{cts}}\to B_Y$, namely $i_Y$ after the continuous comparison and $c_p\circ p^{-1}i_X$, are equal. A map into the limit $B_Y$ is determined by its projections, and by the adjunction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] a map out of $p^{-1}A_X^{\mathrm{cts}}$ is determined by its adjoint on sections $s\in A_X^{\mathrm{cts}}(U)$. After composing with the $n$-th projection and the identification $q_{Y,n}$ of step 2, both send $s$, pulled back to $U\times_XY$, to the function whose value at a point is the residue modulo $\varpi^{n+1}$ of the value of $s$ at the image point: for the first map this is the projection equation on $Y$; for the second it is the projection equation on $X$, once $q_{Y,n}\circ c_{p,n}$ equals the pulled-back $q_{X,n}$ followed by the continuous comparison. Those two maps out of $p^{-1}$ of a constant sheaf agree because both send each constant section to the constant function with the same value (the constant-section equations on $X$ and $Y$). Localizing at $\varpi$ as in step 3 gives the same compatibility between $p^{-1}E_X^{\mathrm{cts}}\simeq E_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}$ and $p^{-1}R_X\simeq R_Y$. Hence the $R_Y$-module $p^{-1}L$ (through $c_p$) is the $E_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}$-module $L|_Y$ of step 7 (through $i_Y$).

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2) on Y and its compatibility with restriction to the etale Y; Definition 6.8.1 (sheaves of continuous functions)

proof.text: Use the identifications of step 8. Give $M$ its $B_Y$-action via $i_Y^{-1}$; the same finite local bases now make it lisse over $B_Y$. On presheaf tensors, the coefficient identifications send $b\otimes m$ to the corresponding rational coefficient tensored with $m$, with inverse given by the inverse ring isomorphisms. The balanced relations are identical because the integral inclusions commute. Sheafifying these inverse maps gives $B_Y[1/\varpi]\otimes_{B_Y}M\simeq E_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}\otimes_{A_Y^{\mathrm{cts}}}M$ by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Composing with $\alpha$ and the identification of $p^{-1}L$ in step 8 gives $M[1/\varpi]\simeq p^{-1}L$ as $R_Y$-modules. Reversing these coefficient actions gives the converse formulation. No gluing on $Y\times_XY$ has been introduced.
